name: Heberprot-P

lead: Heberprot-P is an epidermal growth factor injection made in Cuba to treat severe diabetic foot ulcers.
Human reports are mostly small series and one registered phase 3 trial. No studies of cosmetic use were found.

paras: EGF stimulates skin cell growth. In patients with ulcers it is injected into the wound base and edges to promote granulation tissue.
It is a medical product given by clinicians, not approved in the US as of 2016 per Wikipedia. Safety information in the sources reviewed is limited.

lead: Heberprot-P is an injectable formulation of recombinant human epidermal growth factor (rhEGF, nepidermin) developed by Cuba's Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology and marketed by Heber Biotec. It is used for advanced diabetic foot ulcers, where it is injected into and around the wound[1].

It is a wound-healing medicine. Its relevance to appearance culture is as an EGF product discussed among growth-factor skin and regeneration interests; no studies of it for cosmetic outcomes were found.
infobox: Not approved in the US as of 2016

paras: Heberprot-P is used for deep diabetic foot ulcers, including ischemic ones, with the aim of promoting granulation and closure and reducing amputation risk [1]. Wikipedia reports sale in 23 countries as of 2016 and unavailability in the United States.

A pilot study of 20 diabetic patients with full-thickness ulcers followed intralesional treatment up to complete wound closure [2]. A similar study of 17 patients reported granulation and closure outcomes [3]. A review of 12 limb-threatening ischemic lesions in 11 patients in Turkey examined whether the injections could avoid major amputation [4]. A Cuban review describes it as a product for advanced ulcers [1].

A phase 3 placebo-controlled trial of 304 participants (NCT02554851) was registered in 2017 with unknown status [5]; a 50-patient trial in Kuwait has been completed [6]. A 2022 zebrafish study compared it with another EGF product [7]. Most published human reports are small, uncontrolled series.
Safety data in the sources reviewed are limited; trial registrations list efficacy and safety as outcomes [5][6].

timeline.event: Preparations for US phase 3 trial begin (per Wikipedia).
